question: A wind-tunnel logbook ends with one figure in kilojoules. A model of mass 32 kg is released at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the slope of the curve y = 5x^3 + 1x^2 at x = 2. The energy the moving model carries is the raw reading, to which 10 J stored in the release catch is added. The logbook writes that sum in kilojoules. Nine releases make a campaign, so the campaign figure is 9 times the record, and 8 is then added in those same kilojoule units for the instrumentation. The tunnel's settling chamber holds 900 L of air, which is not used here. What figure ends the logbook, in kJ?

A velodrome audit ends with one figure in kilojoules. The test sled's mass plate reads 12000 g. The sled's speed, in metres per second, is how fast the slope of the curve y = 3x^3 - 4x^2 is itself changing at x = 3. The energy the moving sled carries is the base value, which the audit records in kilojoules. Eight sleds run per session, and the venue holds 7 identical sessions. The track surface is 42 mm thick, which is irrelevant here. What figure ends the audit, in kJ?

A cargo-lift report ends with one number in kilojoules. A cage of mass 42 kg moves at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 5x between x = 2 and x = 3. The energy the moving cage carries is the raw reading, to which 4 J stored in the buffer is added. The report writes that sum in kilojoules, then subtracts 17 in those same kilojoule units as the machine-room allowance. What number ends the report, in kJ?

A dockside test rolls a drum of mass 41 kg down a ramp. Its speed, in metres per second, is the larger root of x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0. The energy the moving drum carries is the base value. Two drums are rolled in each test, so the test energy is 2 times that base value, and the sheet records the total in kilojoules. Two allowances are then added in those same kilojoule units: 20 for the ramp gear and 20 for the catch net. The dock crane's jib is 24 m long, which is not needed. What does the sheet finally record, in kJ?

A bobsled push-start rig launches a sled whose mass plate reads 13000 g. The starting number is the larger root of x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0, and multiplying that root by 3 gives the sled's speed, in metres per second. The energy the moving sled carries is the raw reading, to which 18 J stored in the push handle is added. Twelve pushes make a training block, so the block figure is 12 times that corrected value. The ice house is held at 4 degrees Celsius, which is not part of the calculation. What is the block figure, in J?

A laboratory launcher takes the exact area under the curve y = 5x^2 + 0x between x = 0 and x = 1, then adds 19 to that area. The result is the speed, in metres per second, of a puck of mass 15 kg. The energy the moving puck carries is the raw reading, to which 18 J stored in the launch spring is added. Nine pucks are fired in a session, so the session energy is 9 times that corrected single-puck value. The bench also carries a 5 L solvent bottle that plays no part. What is the session energy, in J?

A quarry haul report ends with one number in joules. A wagon whose mass plate reads 51000 g rolls at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 6x between x = 0 and x = 4. The energy the moving wagon carries is the base value. Ten wagons make a train and 12 trains run in a shift, so the shift energy is 10 times the base value and then 12 times that. From the shift total 19 J is subtracted for the weighbridge gear. What number ends the report, in J?

A rowing club's summary ends with one number in kilojoules. The coach writes out 2k - 1 for k running from 1 to 5 and adds the five values together, and that sum is the boat's speed in metres per second. The boat's mass plate reads 45000 g, and the energy it carries at that speed is the raw reading, from which 26 J is subtracted for hull drag. Four boats race in a heat, so the heat energy is 4 times the corrected single-boat value, and 9 J is then added for the starting gate. The summary writes the result in kilojoules. The boathouse holds 300 L of rainwater, which is not relevant. What number ends the summary, in kJ?

A shipyard rig drives a carriage whose mass plate reads 162000 g. The control curve is y = 3x^3 - 5x^2, and the acceleration given to the carriage, in metres per second squared, is how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 4. The drive must supply the force that gives the carriage that acceleration, and the log writes that force in kilonewtons. Three carriages run per track and 9 tracks run in the yard, so the yard demand is 3 times the logged value and then 9 times that. From the yard total 30 is subtracted, in those same kilonewton units, as the standing tare. A 55 L paint drum stands by the track and is not involved. What is the final figure, in kN?

A laboratory summary ends with one number in kilojoules. A cart whose mass plate reads 54000 g rolls along a track at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 3x between x = 0 and x = 1. The energy the moving cart carries is the raw reading, to which 1 J stored in the bumper is added. The summary writes that sum in kilojoules. Ten carts are run in the experiment, so the experiment figure is 10 times the record. What number ends the summary, in kJ?

A theme-park engineering report ends with a single figure in kilojoules. A gondola of mass 8 kg on the scale model runs at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 5x^2 + 7x between x = 0 and x = 2. The energy one moving gondola carries is the base value. Three gondolas hang from a spoke, so a spoke's energy is 3 times the base value, and the report writes that in kilojoules. A wheel has 12 spokes, and the park has 6 identical wheels. A 200 L ballast tank sits in the hub and is not used. What figure ends the report, in kJ?

A joinery audit ends with one number in kilonewtons. Two batches of 46 and 12 identical panels are stacked into equal full piles, using the largest pile size that divides both counts exactly. A carriage of mass 167 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pile size. The saw drive must supply the force that gives the carriage that acceleration, and the audit records that force in kilonewtons. To the record 25 is added, in those same kilonewton units, as the clamp preload. Eleven carriages run per shop, and the firm has 5 shops. What number ends the audit, in kN?

A print works groups two orders of 323 and 183 identical sheets into equal full bundles, using the largest bundle size that divides both counts exactly. Multiplying that bundle size by 2 gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of the feed carriage. The carriage's mass plate reads 44000 g, and the feed motor must supply the force that gives it that acceleration. The log records that force in kilonewtons. Four carriages run per press, and the works has 6 presses. What is the works total, in kN?

A workshop record ends with one number in kilonewtons. A slide of mass 33 kg is accelerated along its ways. That acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the exact area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 2x between x = 1 and x = 3. The drive must supply the force that gives the slide that acceleration. From that force 13 N is subtracted for the way friction and a further 15 N for the counterbalance, and the remainder is written in kilonewtons. The workshop's air receiver holds 90 L, which is not needed. What number ends the record, in kN?

A test-cell report ends with one number in newtons. A slide whose mass plate reads 36000 g is driven along its rail. The control curve is y = 5x^3 + 4x^2, and the acceleration applied to the slide, in metres per second squared, is the slope of that curve at x = 1. The rail motor must supply the force that gives the slide that acceleration. Nine slides run per cell and 6 cells run in the building, so the building force is 9 times one slide's force and then 6 times that. From the building total 9 N is subtracted for the anchor tare. What number ends the report, in N?

A pottery record ends with one number in kilojoules. Two lots of 391 and 275 identical tiles are packed into equal full crates, using the largest crate size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley of mass 56 kg is then pushed at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that crate size. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value, which the record writes in kilojoules. To that record 11 is added for the kiln door gear and 11 is then subtracted for the meter tare, both in those same kilojoule units. What number ends the record, in kJ?

A ski-lift maintenance test uses a carrier of mass 54 kg. The control number is the larger root of x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0, and multiplying that root by 9 gives the carrier's speed in metres per second. The energy the moving carrier carries is the raw reading, from which 29 J is subtracted for sheave friction. The record writes the remainder in kilojoules. Five carriers are tested in the session, so the session figure is 5 times that record. The drive house holds 80 L of gear oil, which is not part of the test. What is the session figure, in kJ?

A cement works audit ends with one number in newtons. A hopper of mass 69 kg is accelerated on its rail at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0. The drive must supply the force that gives that hopper that acceleration, and 18 N of clamp preload is added to it. Eight hoppers run per line, 10 lines run per works, and the group has 3 identical works. A 400 L water bowser stands in the yard and is not involved. What number ends the audit, in N?

A karting circuit tests a kart whose mass plate reads 53000 g. The control number is the larger root of x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0, and multiplying that root by 5 gives the kart's speed in metres per second. The energy the moving kart carries is the base value. Four karts run in a heat, so a heat's energy is 4 times the base value. Four heats make up the meeting. What is the meeting energy, in J?

An archery club's tally ends with one number in joules. The control number is the larger root of x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0; multiplying that root by 7 and then subtracting 12 gives the bolt's speed in metres per second. The training bolt has a mass of 7 kg, and the energy it carries at that speed is the base value. Two bolts are loosed in each end, so an end's energy is 2 times the base value. To that total 22 J is added for the energy still stored in the bow limbs. What number ends the tally, in J?

A laboratory sheet begins with a control number: the larger root of x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0. Subtracting 8 from that number and then adding 25 gives the speed, in metres per second, of a glider whose mass plate reads 14000 g. The energy the moving glider carries is the base value. Twelve gliders are launched in the run, so the run energy is 12 times that base value. What is the run energy, in J?

A rolling-mill sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. A slab whose mass plate reads 136000 g is accelerated on the run-out table. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 4 multiplied by the sum of 9 and 7. The rollers must supply the force that gives the slab that acceleration. Three tables work in parallel, so the mill force is 3 times one table's figure, and 30 N of drive preload is added to it. The sheet writes that in kilonewtons and then adds 23 in those same kilonewton units for the stand tare. A 250 L coolant sump serves the mill and is not involved. What number ends the sheet, in kN?

A tile depot groups two deliveries of 246 and 137 identical slabs into equal full pallets, using the largest pallet size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 147000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pallet size. The pusher must supply the force that gives the trolley that acceleration, and 6 N of spring preload is added to it. The log writes that loaded force in kilonewtons. Eleven trolleys run per aisle, and the depot has 3 aisles. A 90 L grout tub stands at the end of the aisle and is not involved. What is the depot total, in kN?

A conveyor at a bottling plant drives a carriage of mass 117 kg. The control number is the larger root of x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, and multiplying that root by 5 gives the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared. The belt must supply the force that gives the carriage that acceleration. From that force 17 N is subtracted for the roller drag. The log records the remainder in kilonewtons. What does the log record, in kN?

A model railway club rolls a wagon of mass 5 kg along the test track. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0. The energy the moving wagon carries is the base value. Seven wagons make a rake, 10 rakes make a layout, 11 layouts are on show, and the exhibition tours 3 venues. The clubhouse has a 20 L water butt that plays no part. What is the exhibition total, in J?
